newsitem.title: CHINA: Fangda sees 50 pct rise in 1997 H1 net.
newsitem.headline: Fangda sees 50 pct rise in 1997 H1 net.

text.p: Chinese building materials producer Shenzhen Fangda Industrial Co Ltd expects to see a year-on-year jump of about 50 percent in net profits for first-half 1997, a company official said on Monday.
The earnings advance was fuelled by robust demand for the company's core product, curtain wall glass, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Fangda posted net profits of 45.08 million yuan (US$5.43 million) for January-June 1996 based on Chinese accounting standards.
Under international standards, it booked 44.02 million yuan in net profits for the period.
Fangda had used proceeds from a recent additional B share offer to expand production of curtain wall glass, the official said.

Fangda, which listed 30 million new B shares at HK$8.50 each last month, aimed to boost annual curtain wall glass production capacity to 350,000 square metres (3.767 million sq ft) from the present 150,000 square metres (1.614 million sq ft), the official said.
The expansion would lay down a solid foundation for Fangda's profit growth in the future, he said but gave no further details.
Fangda posted net profits of 107.9 million yuan for 1996 against 42.1 million in 1995 based on international standards. It attributed earnings growth to increased sales.
China's top brokerage Shenyin & Wanguo Securities recently recommended Fangda's B shares as a "buy", saying Fangda was set to expand strongly in the next two years.
The brokerage said in a research paper that Fangda's products, particularly curtain wall glass, were eligible for special support from the central government, but it gave no details.
